title: Characters and bytes
description:
Compare the size of text in UTF-8 and UTF-16, the two encodings Windows programs meet.

```
"Hello"   UTF-8 5 bytes, UTF-16 10 bytes, 5 characters
"Grüße"   UTF-8 7 bytes, UTF-16 10 bytes, 5 characters
"日本"     UTF-8 6 bytes, UTF-16 4 bytes, 2 characters
"😀"      UTF-8 4 bytes, UTF-16 4 bytes (2 units), 1 character
```
hints: `(static_cast<unsigned char>(c) & 0xC0) != 0x80` is true for the first byte of each character (lesson 5.03).
A 4-byte UTF-8 sequence starts with `11110xxx`, and those are the code points that need two UTF-16 units.
requirements: Count code points in UTF-8 by skipping continuation bytes (`10xxxxxx`).
Work out UTF-16 sizes from the code points (2 bytes, or 4 above 0xFFFF).
Print a table for a few strings.
stretch: Convert with `MultiByteToWideChar` on Windows and check your counts.
